feed.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories
feed.subtitle: Top stories in the U.S. and world news, politics, health, science, business, music, arts and culture. Nonprofit journalism with a mission. This is NPR.

entry.title: How a bank collapse left millions in limbo and toppled Paraguay's president
entry.summary: A bank's collapse in Paraguay left millions locked out of their money, toppled the president and exposed a web of political and financial ties.

entry.title: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO's alleged relationship with Chinese spy
entry.summary: The chipmaking giant says it is looking into reports by The New York Times that its CEO, Jensen Huang, was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation.

entry.title: NASA is looking for astronauts to live and work on the Moon
entry.summary: NASA needs more recruits in order to return to the moon after being gone more than half a century.

entry.title: Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections
entry.summary: France says European officials will attend this week's U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, the first three-way round of negotiations since February.

entry.title: No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks
entry.summary: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, who will lead a caretaker government while negotiations take place, said: "I think everyone's over politics so let's all have a bit of a break for the next three weeks".

entry.title: After a successful trip to Uruguay, Pope Leo heads to Argentina
entry.summary: On Sunday, tens of thousands packed the main square in Florida, Uruguay, to watch Pope Leo speak.

entry.title: Russell Brand to learn sentence after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault
entry.summary: Comedian Brand faces a "significant" prison sentence, which a London court judge is set to hand down on Monday.

entry.title: Climate change is altering the colors we see in the world: an illustrated journey
entry.summary: From Arctic landscapes to insect bodies, climate change is shifting the familiar colors of nature.

entry.title: One air ambulance service rethinks what it takes to practice medicine in the sky
entry.summary: Air medical service comes with high risks, high costs, and staffing struggles. To reduce turnover and serve rural patients, LifeFlight of Maine is putting the needs of healthcare workers first.

entry.title: A desert stirs to life: Chile's Atacama erupts in its biggest floral display in decades
entry.summary: El Niño rains have transformed Chile's Atacama Desert into a spectacular sea of color, awakening a fleeting ecosystem of flowers and wildlife in one of the driest places on Earth.
